newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves tighter law to police finance firms.
newsitem.headline: India approves tighter law to police finance firms.

text.p: The Indian cabinet approved on Friday a proposal to issue an ordinance to amend the law to step up regulation of non-banking financial companies, the United News of India (UNI) said.

"The cabinet...cleared a proposal to promulgate an ordinance for amending the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act of 1934 for regulating the activities of non-banking and unincorporated bodies," the news agency said.
"This would enable better regulation of the activities of the non-banking financial companies and unincorporated bodies," UNI said.
An ordinance, or a presidential decree passed after a cabinet approval is a law that comes into immediate effect, but it must be later approved by parliament.

The Indian government has been considering tighter regulation of non-banking finance companies by the central bank after some unregistered finance companies defaulted in redeeming deposits made by customers.
